name: Snow Pudding I
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer (1896)
steps: Soak gelatine in cold water, dissolve in boiling water, add sugar and lemon juice, strain, and set aside in cool place; occasionally stir mixture, and when quite thick, beat with wire spoon or whisk until frothy; add whites of eggs beaten stiff, and continue beating until stiff enough to hold its shape.
Mould, or pile by spoonfuls on glass dish; serve cold with Boiled Custard.
A very attractive dish may be prepared by coloring half the mixture with fruit red.

culture.text: From The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) by Fannie Merritt Farmer. It popularized level, standardized measurements (cups and spoons) in American home kitchens, and stayed one of the best-selling cookbooks in the United States for decades.
